what: Touch B: the blocks of one lesson (lessons-site lesson-model/1) and of one book companion (design note), with a real example each. Text is ours, from the cited sources.

blocks.title: Watch: a short video
blocks.holds: A Manim animation of the one idea, rendered off the Mac. Final videos run 36 to 48 seconds, without sound.
blocks.example: The VC-dimension video was rendered again so that it says the curve is consistent with the bound, the same words as the lesson text.
blocks.reach: The app plays the local video file with its poster. A lesson without its file shows "video pending".

blocks.title: Touch: an interactive on real data
blocks.holds: A small widget that changes one thing and shows one effect, on a real data set or the book's own example. A "Show the code" panel holds its JavaScript and the Python that made its data.
blocks.example: Drag 3 to 5 points: the widget tests every dichotomy exactly, so you see m(4) = 14 < 16. A second view puts the CS 156 digits 1 vs 5 learning curve against the VC bound.
blocks.reach: In the app the widget runs in a sandboxed frame: it cannot read the app's cookies, storage or page.

blocks.title: The same idea in each book
blocks.holds: One row per book: notation, formula, viewpoint and assumptions, side by side. On a phone, one card per book.
blocks.example: VC dimension is covered by 5 of the 9 books.
blocks.reach: Formulas render with KaTeX. A click on a cell's source opens that book at the page.

blocks.title: Explain, in layers
blocks.holds: The idea at three depths. Each layer, takeaway and caveat says which page or lecture moment it comes from, or that it is our own.
blocks.example: The growth function m(N) = N² − N + 2 had no page, so m(4) = 14 is now cited to LFD p.55 and the general formula is marked as our enumeration.
blocks.reach: Select any text and press "Ask about this": it fills the chat box with the excerpt; it sends nothing until you send it.

blocks.title: Practice
blocks.holds: Multiple-choice items with an explanation for each answer.
blocks.example: One VC-dimension item had two right answers; the other-family check found it and the item was fixed.
blocks.reach: The server scores the answers against the lesson's own items and keeps your best score. Bands: green at 80 % or more, yellow from 50 %, red under 50 %.

blocks.title: Sources, opened in place
blocks.holds: Every book page and lecture moment the lesson uses.
blocks.example: A book source opens the local PDF at the page with the cited section boxed; a lecture source plays the local video at the minute.
blocks.reach: Learn-first links come from the knowledge graph only when at least 2 prerequisite edges agree; a single edge is a lighter "see also".

views.label: Book companion, one per chapter
views.example: Hands-On Large Language Models, chapter 3 (the pilot), pp. 73-107

blocks.title: Reading map
blocks.holds: A small graph: the chapter's sections, the key ideas they hold, and the prerequisites from earlier chapters or other books (dashed). A click on a node jumps to its block.
blocks.example: The structure comes from the book's table of contents by script; a model drafts the idea-to-prerequisite edges.
blocks.reach: You open the companion next to the book you are reading.

blocks.title: Key idea blocks: Watch, Touch, Check
blocks.holds: 4 to 10 per chapter. Each has a layered explanation, a Watch clip (Manim, 60 to 120 seconds), a Touch interactive, a Check quiz and "Read it: pp. N-M".
blocks.example: The pilot chapter covers transformer internals, decoding, the KV cache and attention.
blocks.reach: Each block points back to the book pages it explains.

blocks.title: Play: a sandbox
blocks.holds: Sliders over a real formula, a small JavaScript model, a Python cell we wrote, or a "build it" board for architecture chapters. Some chapters get none.
blocks.example: Process and architecture books get build-it boards more than formulas.
blocks.reach: In the page; a Python cell is ready to run on Colab.

blocks.title: Chapter check
blocks.holds: 5 to 10 questions over the whole chapter, each option with its explanation, each question naming the page its answer rests on.
blocks.example: No question copies a book exercise.
blocks.reach: In the page, in the browser.

blocks.title: Sources and the copy rules
blocks.holds: Every claim with its book page. The text is in our own words; a quote is at most 25 words, with its page.
blocks.example: A script checks each claim's anchor on its page, and every 8-word run against the chapter; a model of another family reads claim and page.
blocks.reach: Book text never leaves the machine.

blocks.title: Link to the tutor
blocks.holds: The same unit ids and graph relations as the tutor: key ideas as Concept nodes, Check items as non-gold exercises, Watch and Touch as assets the tutor can attach to an answer.
blocks.example: A wrong answer would tell the tutor which concept to revisit and which clip to show.
blocks.reach: Planned: the companions are not yet wired into the tutor app.
